Impetuous

im-PECH-oo-uhs · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Impetuous is acting or done suddenly, with little thought for the consequences.

His impetuous decision to skip the safety briefing nearly cost him his footing on the cliff trail.

Worked Example

Impetuous as ever, the young knight charged the enemy line alone before his captain could finish giving orders.

He acted the instant an impulse struck, without pausing to weigh the risk, which is the hallmark of impetuous behavior.

How Impetuous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

impulsive

impulsive: acting suddenly, without thinking things through

rash

rash: acting without careful consideration of the consequences

Antonyms

cautious

cautious: careful to avoid danger or mistakes

deliberate

deliberate: done consciously and carefully, after consideration

How Strong Is It? — spontaneous → impetuous → reckless

spontaneous vs. impetuous

spontaneous vs. impetuous: done without prior planning, but not necessarily reckless

reckless vs. impetuous

reckless vs. impetuous: utterly without regard for consequences or safety

Build the Word

The pieces

root — impetus

root — impetus: a force or influence that gets something moving or started (from Latin impetus, 'an attack, force, impulse') (Latin impetus)

suffix — -uous

suffix — -uous: possessing the quality of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Impetuous is impetus ('a driving force or sudden impulse') plus -uous, 'full of.' Someone impetuous is full of that sudden impulse, acting on it before stopping to think.

Use the root in a new word: impetus

Use the root in a new word: impetus: The coach's halftime speech provided the impetus the team needed to storm back in the second half.
